ledger.reason: CLM-002 was denied CO-16 with M76 (missing diagnosis) and MA130. Its 84443 line had an empty diagnosis pointer list. Both paid CASCADE claims point every line to at least one diagnosis, so no paid claim matches. The cause is the missing pointer, not the lab code or the E/M on the same claim, so the rule applies to any CPT. It sets no POS, plan or day-count condition. The days_to_submit evidence (denied at 2, paid up to 6) is unrelated to this cause.

ledger.reason: Timely filing: the gate accepts any cutoff above 3 (max paid) and at or below 204 (min CARC-29 denial). I chose 90, a common commercial filing limit, rather than the bare minimum of 3, which would be implausible. Modifier: the claim with 59 on 97164 was denied CO-4/N823, while the same claim pattern with XU was paid. That points to a policy against 59 in favor of the X modifiers. No paid claim carries 59, so I kept the rule general rather than limiting it to therapy codes. Exception: the out-of-network 99203 was paid. Both denied claims are in-network, so the rule 'in_network false gives paid' contradicts no denial. I kept it general rather than limiting it to E/M codes.

Northstar rejects modifier 59 as a distinct-service modifier and requires the X{EPSU} subset instead, denying any line billed with 59 under CARC 4 (N823).

ledger.reason: R-003 is the only active rule, so there is nothing to merge. It is already about as general as the evidence allows. It covers the full office E/M range (99202-99215) and the full immunization administration range (90460-90474), and it does not require the vaccine product code or particular diagnoses. Both denied claims (CLM-012, CLM-027) have an E/M line but no immunization administration line, so the rule correctly does not fire on them. Dropping the E/M condition would also pass the replay check, but it would turn an E/M modifier-25 exception into a blanket 'paid' override for any claim with immunization administration. That goes beyond the policy the evidence supports, so I kept the rule unchanged.

R-004 is the only active rule and is already as general as the evidence allows. Its single substantive condition is that some line has fewer than 1 diagnosis pointer. That describes the policy directly and has no code to widen into a family or range. It fires on denied CLM-002, whose line 84443 has no pointers. It does not fire on paid CLM-010 or CLM-018, where every line has pointers. The payer=CASCADE condition only matches the rule's payer scope, so removing it would not generalize anything. There are no other rules to merge.

No replacement is proposed; each rule is already as general as the evidence allows. The three rules describe different policies (CARC 29 timely filing, CARC 4 modifier 59, and a paid exception for out-of-network claims), so none can be merged. R-006 and R-007 have only the payer condition plus one essential condition, with no code to widen. For R-005, the paid claims would technically allow a threshold as low as days_to_submit > 3, but the 90-day limit is the stated policy. Lowering it on such sparse evidence would wrongly deny timely claims.

There are now 2 paid BAYVIEW claims (CLM-017 and CLM-022), so I am retrying the two rules the gate previously rejected for insufficient evidence.

1. **POS 02 at home (CARC 5):** I kept the POS 02 plus patient-at-home pairing. That pairing is the actual inconsistency; POS 02 alone is valid when the patient is not at home. Neither paid claim is POS 02.
2. **Timely filing (CARC 29):** The cutoff is days_to_submit > 90. It sits above the largest paid value (4) and below the CARC 29 denial (105), and matches the usual 90-day limit.
3. **Zero charge (CARC 16):** The rule fires on any line with charge <= 0. The lowest paid line charge is 30.
4. **Out of network (CARC 242):** The rule fires when in_network is false. There are no paid out-of-network BAYVIEW claims. A referral on file did not prevent the denial, so the rule does not check referrals.

No replacements proposed. The five rules cover five separate policies (CARC 5, 16, 29, 242, plus the paid exception), so nothing can be merged. R-003: both the E/M and immunization-admin ranges are needed. Dropping the immunization condition would make the rule fire on denied E/M claims CLM-012, CLM-027 and CLM-029. Dropping the E/M condition would turn the modifier-25 exception into a different policy. R-008: POS 02 is valid when the patient is not at home, so the home-location condition is part of the policy. The evidence does not justify dropping it. R-009: the 90-day limit already sits between the highest paid value (4 days) and the lowest CARC 29 denial (105 days), and it matches the stated filing limit. R-010 and R-011 are already single-condition rules.

No replacements proposed. R-004 (CARC 16) and R-012 (CARC 167) predict different CARCs for unrelated causes, so they cannot be merged. R-004 already covers any line with no diagnosis pointer, which is as general as the policy allows. R-012 names a single code, 82306 (25-hydroxy vitamin D), but no wider range is safe. The nearby code 82652 (1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D) has different coverage indications, and nothing in the evidence supports widening to a range. R-012's covered-diagnosis exclusion list is what the policy itself turns on. Dropping it would deny 82306 claims with covered indications, so it stays.

R-015's description states a CT/MRI/PET prior-auth policy, but the rule only matches head/neck codes 70450-70559. The replacement widens it to CT/MRI/PET code prefixes across body regions. Prefixes that would catch plain-film x-rays are avoided: 72120-72124 and 72190 are excluded by listing exact codes instead. Coverage is kept: CLM-030 (70551, no auth) still matches. It does not fire on any paid claim: CLM-028 (72148) has prior auth on file. The other rules are a single example each, with no sibling rules to merge and no wider family the evidence supports. R-005, R-006, R-007 and R-014 are already minimal, so they are left unchanged.

ledger.reason: CLM-021 is a 97110 therapy claim denied with CARC 119 and N362 at visit_count_ytd 20. The only paid claim with a visit count is CLM-020 at 9, so any cutoff from 10 to 20 fits the evidence. I chose gte 20 because a 20-visit annual therapy cap is the usual plan design. Strictly, the most general cutoff the evidence allows is gte 10, so this choice is a judgement call. The CPT condition covers the whole physical medicine and rehab family (97010-97799) rather than just 97110. No GP modifier, place of service or diagnosis condition is added, because no paid counterexample requires one. CLM-026 is a therapy claim at visit 6, but it was denied under CARC 4 for modifier 59, which is a separate cause.

ledger.reason:
No replacements proposed. Every active rule covers a different policy with a different CARC or outcome (5, 29, 16, 242, 97, and the paid exception), so nothing can be merged. Each rule is already at the right level of generality.

- R-003 already uses full ranges: E/M 99202-99215 and immunization admin 90460-90474. Dropping the immunization condition would make it fire on denied claims CLM-012, CLM-027 and CLM-029. Dropping the E/M condition would no longer describe the modifier-25 policy.
- R-008: patient_location=home is the cause of the denial, since POS 02 is valid for non-home telehealth. Keeping it is policy-justified.
- R-009 uses the stated 90-day limit, which falls between the paid maximum (4 days) and the denied minimum (105 days).
- R-010 and R-011 are single-condition rules.
- R-024 already uses the specimen-collection range 36415-36416 and the clinical lab range 80047-89398.

No replacements proposed. The three active rules each have a different CARC and cause (16 missing diagnosis pointer, 167 non-covered vitamin D diagnosis, 4 missing modifier 25), so none can be merged.

- **R-004:** It is already a single condition with no code restriction.
- **R-012:** It stays limited to CPT 82306, the 25-hydroxy vitamin D test. 82652 (1,25-dihydroxy vitamin D) has different coverage indications, and no claim supports widening to it. The covered-diagnosis exclusion list is what defines the policy. Dropping it would replay cleanly, since no paid claim has a vitamin D line, but it would wrongly deny vitamin D tests that do have a covered indication.
- **R-025:** It already spans the full office/outpatient E/M range (99202-99215) and the full drug/injection administration family (96360-96549). Both remaining conditions do real work. The missing-modifier-25 condition is the cause of the denial. The administration-code condition keeps the rule off paid CLM-014 (99214 alone, no modifier) and CLM-040 (E/M with modifier 25 plus a biopsy). Widening to minor procedures or other E/M families is not supported by any denial.

No replacement is proposed; each active rule already describes one distinct policy at the breadth the evidence supports. CARC 119 appears in two rules, but they have different causes and are not merged. R-014 is the preventive-visit frequency limit (CPT 99381-99397, fewer than 365 days since the last preventive visit). R-026 is the therapy visit cap (97010-97799, year-to-date visits of 20 or more). They also could not be written as one AND-only rule. R-005 (more than 90 days to submit), R-014 (fewer than 365 days) and R-026 (20 or more visits) use the payer's policy thresholds. The evidence would technically allow looser thresholds, such as more than 3 days or 10 or more visits, but those would be overfit guesses that hold valid claims. R-023 already covers the full CT/MRI/PET code families, and it needs its prior-auth-missing condition because paid claim CLM-028 is a 72148 MRI with an authorization on file. R-006 and R-007 are already minimal.
